definitions.business_name: An identifying name of a company, organization, commercial establishment or service provider expressed in that organizational, merchant or provider role. A named transportation provider can satisfy both business_name and transport_agency from the same expressed provider relation. Physical product-brand modification or software access alone does not establish an organization/provider role. Apply expressed-communicative-content scope.
definitions.business_type: An expressed category of commercial establishment or offered service. A transportation service requested or described as a service, such as booking a taxi or flight, can satisfy this predicate together with transport_type. A vehicle category, physical facility or place alone does not establish a commercial service role. Apply expressed-communicative-content scope.
definitions.transport_agency: An identifying name of an organization or service expressed as providing transportation. The transportation-provider relation must be supported by the utterance; a brand in a stock query or an application-opening instruction alone does not establish it. The same expressed named provider may also satisfy business_name. Apply expressed-communicative-content scope.

rules: A single expressed named transportation provider may support business_name and transport_agency simultaneously. Distinct predicates do not require distinct mentions or entities. Evaluate the expressed role under each definition; do not propagate a label from a native entity tag or ontology hierarchy.

A name attached to a represented transport service, as in AA flight or Ola cab, may express its operator/provider. In these constructions the provider role is part of the service attribution; no expansion of an acronym, corporate ownership lookup or separate commercial transaction is required. An identifying name is enough; canonical company identity is not an output.

The physical product-brand exclusion concerns a name serving only to identify a physical product, such as Samsung phone or Wemo plug. It does not exclude an explicitly named service operator merely because the name grammatically modifies a service noun. Genuine provider-versus-title/product attachment ambiguity stays unavailable.

Opening or using an app alone does not establish the company or transportation-provider role. A stock/organization query names an organization without necessarily expressing transportation. App access and an explicitly attributed ride can support both software and provider roles; neither role automatically supplies the other.

Bare Uber or find me an Uber without a journey/service or software cue remains ambiguous for provider role; native travel labels and familiar brand knowledge cannot settle it. Book Uber for a time or destination expresses a scheduled named service, but whether transportation is supported must be assessed from the complete wording, not the brand alone.

business_type asks for an establishment or offered-service category, not a provider name. Book a taxi or book a flight expresses a transport-service category and transport_type. A bare vehicle, an airport/gate used only as location, or a flight word inside a museum title does not establish a service category. Do not infer commercial role from hypothetical tickets, payment or infrastructure.

No categorical implication from transport_type to business_type: a car described as a physical object can express mode/category without a offered-service role. No reverse implication from business_name to transport_agency: company stock and complaint contexts need their own transportation evidence.
basis: Clarify generic provider inclusion and independent overlapping role predicates; not native slot-label reproduction or teacher-answer matching.
